haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes unless committed or released first. Then it expires (sweeper, or commit refuses it) and returns to sale. The hold is not extended.
haiku-low.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge (M2 before M4). If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no charge is requested, the order is SHORT_STOCK, and the cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q3: The charge is keyed by order id, and the provider Idempotency-Key is the order id. Payment returns the existing charge for a repeat, so no double charge.
haiku-low.q4: Order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and sends M8. Payment refunds the full charged amount (M12). On M9 the order becomes REFUNDED and the customer is emailed.
haiku-low.q5: The cart is emptied only when Order sends M7 OrderConfirmed, removing the ordered lines by line id. If checkout fails, the cart is left unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service drives the flow. Its orders table stores each checkout's status, and status history is kept in Order's own tables.
haiku-low.q7: Provider webhook (M10) reaches Payment, which commits the outcome and writes an outbox event (M5) to the broker that Order consumes. Reconciliation can feed the same outcome.
haiku-low.q8: Payment's unique provider event id makes a duplicate insert change nothing, and charge updates apply only while PENDING. Order ignores repeats by processed event id.
haiku-low.q9: Payment sets the charge DECLINED and emits M5 PaymentDeclined. Order sets DECLINED and queues M6, which makes Inventory release the reservation.
haiku-low.q10: At commit, Inventory accepts only an ACTIVE, unexpired hold. If refused, the order is cancelled out of stock and refunded. If accepted, it is confirmed. No re-reservation.
haiku-low.q11: The provider says the refund failed. The refund becomes REFUND_FAILED in Payment's refunds table, and its M12 retry is reopened with the count plus one, resent with the same key after backoff. Ops is alerted after 10 tries.
haiku-low.q12: Order's M7 OrderConfirmed event, sent through Order's outbox after confirmation, causes Cart to remove the ordered lines by line id.

sonnet.q1: 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 min). If not committed or released, the Inventory sweeper (every minute) marks ACTIVE reservations past expires_at as EXPIRED, and commit also checks expires_at itself and refuses. The stock then returns to sale. The hold is not extended.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved first (M2), before the charge (M4 is sent only after AWAITING_PAYMENT). If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing (all lines in one transaction), Order becomes SHORT_STOCK, no payment is requested, the customer sees the short items, and the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q3: Idempotency by order id. Payment's charge row is keyed by order id and returns the existing charge for a repeated M4, and the provider call M11 uses Idempotency-Key = order id. Retries reuse the same order id, so no second charge.
sonnet.q4: The commit (M3) is refused, so Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and sends M8 through its outbox. Payment creates a refund row and refunds the full charged amount (M12). When M9 RefundCompleted arrives, the order becomes REFUNDED and an email is queued. Customer sees 'cancelled, refund in progress' until then.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only after the order is confirmed: Order sets CONFIRMED and sends M7 OrderConfirmed, and Cart removes the ordered lines (C2). On any failure branch (failed, short stock, declined, cancelled) the cart stays unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Order service drives the flow. The record of progress is Order's orders table status (PLACING, AWAITING_PAYMENT, PAYMENT_RECEIVED, CONFIRMED, etc.), plus status history, order_lines, and its retry queue/outbox.
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook (M10) to Payment, or Payment finds the outcome by reconciliation query after 30 min without a webhook. Payment updates the charge and writes an M5 event (PaymentSucceeded/PaymentDeclined) to its outbox; the relay publishes it on the broker and Order consumes it.
sonnet.q8: Several layers. Payment inserts the unique provider event id, so a duplicate webhook fails the insert and does nothing (returns 200); the charge update applies only while still PENDING. Order records processed event ids (M5, M9) and ignores repeats by event id. Refund updates apply unless already REFUNDED, so no second M9.
sonnet.q9: Order sets DECLINED upon receiving M5 PaymentDeclined and queues M6 (release reservation) in its retry queue in the same step. Inventory marks the reservation RELEASED. The cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q10: It does not decide on the payment; it attempts the commit (M3) after PaymentSucceeded. Inventory accepts only if the reservation is ACTIVE and not past expires_at. If refused (for any reason), the order is CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and the full amount is refunded; if accepted, the order is CONFIRMED. No re-reservation.
sonnet.q11: If the provider reports REFUND_FAILED, the refund row becomes REFUND_FAILED and its M12 row in Payment's retry queue is reopened with attempt count plus one. It is resent with the same key after backoff (1 min doubling to a 1 hour cap), set back to REFUND_PENDING, and never gives up. Ops is alerted after 10 tries. Pending refunds are tracked in Payment's refunds table and retry queue (reconcile_at drives reconciliation). Order is not told of failure.
sonnet.q12: The Order service's confirmation (CONFIRMED) writes an M7 OrderConfirmed event to its outbox; the Cart service consumes it and removes the ordered lines by cart line id (C2). So Cart does the clearing, triggered by Order's M7.
